newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: HK police probe Cambodia immigrant smuggling ring.
newsitem.headline: HK police probe Cambodia immigrant smuggling ring.

text.p: Three Hong Kong police officers flew into Cambodia on Tuesday to help local authorites probe an international ring smuggling Chinese illegal immigrants.
"The Cambodians have got a few people in custody. They're Hong Kong residents and we'd like to talk to them," said Martin Richardson of Hong Kong's Organised Crime and Triad Bureau.
"We try to work together, exchange information about the Chinese connection here in Cambodia," Police General Skadavy M. Ly Roun told Reuters.
Cambodian police on December 25 arrested two suspected Hong Kong leaders of a smuggling ring after finding 78 ethnic Chinese hiding in a Phnom Penh villa.
The syndicate is believed to have moved large numbers of Chinese migrants, mostly from mainland China, to the United States, South America, Europe and Africa.
Richardson said the Hong Kong team, in Cambodia for three days, would also seek to determine if and when suspects would be brought to court and on what charges.
News reports in Hong Kong have said thousands of illegal immigrants from China have paid $30,000 each to be smuggled abroad.
Skadavy M. Ly Roun said earlier this month there were about 10,000 illegal ethnic Chinese immigrants in Cambodia.
